key_insight: Vega trains an instruction-conditioned vision–language–action model using a large, instruction-annotated driving dataset so vehicles can follow diverse natural-language driving commands for personalized behavior.
problem_solved: Existing vision–language driving pipelines only use language for descriptions or reasoning and cannot flexibly execute diverse user instructions; this work enables explicit instruction following and personalized driving policies.
method: Construct InstructScene: a large-scale dataset (~100k scenes) pairing rich natural-language driving instructions with corresponding trajectories/actions.
Train a multimodal model that aligns visual observations, language instructions, and action sequences to learn instruction-conditioned driving policies.
Evaluate instruction-following performance across realistic driving scenarios to demonstrate flexible, personalized behavior driven by natural language.
impact: Provides a concrete dataset and modeling recipe for building instruction-driven autonomous agents, enabling more natural human–vehicle interaction and accelerating research on multimodal, policy-oriented models.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing: camera input + language instruction → multimodal encoder → policy → executed trajectory

paper_title: Vega: Learning to Drive with Natural Language Instructions
paper_authors: Sicheng Zuo, Yuxuan Li, Wenzhao Zheng, Zheng Zhu, Jie Zhou
